title: Fluorescence-microscopy-based assay assessing regulatory mechanisms of global genome nucleotide excision repair in cultured cells
protocol: Trypsinize U2OS cells stably expressing EGFP-XPC and measure the cell density with a hemocytometer.
Plate 3.0 × 10^5 cells per 35 mm glass bottom dish and culture the cells for 16–20 h.
Seed 1.0 × 10^5 cells in a 35 mm glass bottom dish if transient expression of protein is needed, and culture for 16-20 h.
Transfect with 2 μg of the expression construct after culturing for additional 2 days.
Subject cells to local UVC irradiation through polycarbonate isopore membrane filters.
Irradiate the cells with UVC through the filter as described above.
Add 2 mL of the standard growth medium.
Carefully remove the floating filter.
Culture the cells at 37°C for the desired time period.
Wash the cells twice with 1 mL of PBS.
Incubate the cells for 10 min at 25°C with 1 mL of 2% paraformaldehyde.
Wash the cells twice with 1 mL of PBS.
Incubate the cells for 10 min on ice with 1 mL of 0.5% Triton X-100.
Wash the cells twice with 1 mL of PBS.
Incubate the cells for 30 min at 37°C with 1 mL of 20% FBS to block nonspecific antibody binding.
Wash the cells twice with 1 mL of PBS.
Incubate the cells for 16–20 h at 4°C with an appropriate volume of primary antibody solution (e.g., 100 μL for a 14 mm glass bottom hole).
Wash the cells five times with 1 mL of PBS.
Incubate the cells for 30 min at 37°C with an appropriate volume of 5% FBS containing 4 μg/mL Alexa Fluor 594-labeled secondary antibody (e.g., 100 μL for a 14 mm glass bottom hole).
Wash the cells five times with 1 mL of PBS.
Incubate the cells for 10 min at 25°C with 1 mL of PBS containing 1 μg/mL Hoechst 33342.
Wash the cells five times with 1 mL of PBS.
Mount the cells under a round coverslip (11 mm diameter) with 5 μL of the Vectashield mounting medium.
Select a 40× objective lens.
Focus on the sample.
Set three channels for fluorescence images: Hoechst 33342, EGFP, and Alexa Fluor 594.
Set Airy Units to 1.00 AU in all channels.
Set image resolution to 1024 × 1024-pixels with 1× digital zoom (pixel size: 0.31 μm).
Set scan speed to 10 μsec/pixel.
Set LUT to Hi-Lo mode.
Click “Live” to display the fluorescence signals.
Adjust laser powers for Hoechst 33342, EGFP, and Alexa Fluor 594.
Acquire fluorescence images from a single focal plane.
Irradiate U2OSDDB2 KO cells stably expressing EGFP-XPC with UVC (400 J/m²) through the isopore membrane filter.
Incubate irradiated cells for 30 min.
Fix cells after incubation.
Subject fixed cells to immunofluorescence staining with an anti-H3K27ac antibody.
Open the acquired multichannel image with Fiji/ImageJ.
Open ROI manager within Fiji/ImageJ.
Determine and register ROIs by clicking “Add [t]” in ROI manager.
Save the information of registered ROIs by clicking “More” and then “Save…”.
Separate the multichannel image to pick up the signal of Alexa Fluor 594.
Select parameters for image quantification in “Set measurements”.
Obtain quantification data by clicking “Measure”.
Determine three regions of interest in Fiji/ImageJ2: UVC-irradiated area, entire cell nucleus, and background area outside any cells.
Open ROI manager by selecting "Analyze," then "Tools," and finally "ROI Manager."
Choose “Rectangle” for determining the background region or “Polygon selections” for other ROIs.
Add each created ROI to the ROI manager one by one.
Save all registered ROIs after completing their registration in the ROI manager.
Click “Analyze” and then click “Set Measurements…” to select “Area” and “Integrated density.”
Acquire the fluorescence intensity in each ROI by clicking “Measure” in the ROI manager toolbar.
Save the results as a csv file.
Open the results file and copy and paste the data (Label, Area, and Integrated density) into a new Excel file.
Determine the mean fluorescence intensities per pixel by dividing the integrated density by the area in Excel software.
Define the mean fluorescence intensity per pixel corresponding to D, N, and BKG as FD, FN, and FBKG.
Calculate the relative fluorescence intensities at the LUD site (FR) using the formula: FR = (FD - FBKG) / (FN - FBKG).
TrYPsinize U2OS cells and measure the cell density with a hemocytometer.
Plate 3.0 × 10^4 cells per well of a sterile 96-well glass bottom plate.
Culture the cells for 16–20 hours.
Carefully remove the growth medium from a column of wells that are subjected to UVC irradiation using a multichannel micropipette.
Remove the medium from each column of wells.
Irradiate the cells with UVC through the cover of the strip-well plate at a dose of 10 J/m2.
Add 150 μL of fresh growth medium to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for the desired time period.
Transfer the 96-well glass bottom plate on ice after the recovery culture ends.
Prepare the standard curve by irradiating cells kept on ice with UVC doses of 5 and 10 J/m2.
Perform immunofluorescence staining on the whole plate.
Further incubate the plate at 37°C for recovery times of 30, 60, and 120 minutes respectively after UV irradiation.
Transfer the plate on ice.
Remove the medium from three columns of wells containing unirradiated cells.
Irradiate the cells in individual columns with UVC at doses of 5 J/m² and 10 J/m².
Incubate the cells for 10 minutes at 25°C with 2% paraformaldehyde (150 μL per well).
Wash the cells three times with PBS (150 μL per well).
Incubate the cells for 10 minutes at 25°C with PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100 (150 μL per well).
Wash the cells three times with PBS (150 μL per well).
Incubate the cells for 20 min at 25°C in 2 M HCl (150 μL per well).
Wash the cells three times with PBS (150 μL per well).
Add 20% FBS (150 μL per well) to block nonspecific antibody binding.
Incubate the cells for 30 min at 25°C.
Dilute an anti-6-4PP mouse antibody to a final concentration of 0.5 μg/mL with 5% FBS.
Incubate the cells for 16–20 h at 4°C with the primary antibody solution (50 μL per well).
Wash the cells three times with PBS (150 μL per well).
Dilute an Alexa Fluor 405-labeled anti-mouse IgG secondary antibody to a final concentration of 2 μg/mL with 5% FBS.
Incubate the cells for 60 min at 25°C with the secondary antibody solution (50 μL per well).
Wash the cells three times with PBS (150 μL per well).
Stain nuclear DNA for 20 min at 25°C with PBS containing 1 μg/mL propidium iodide (PI) (50 μL per well).
Wash the cells three times with PBS (150 μL per well).
Fill each well with 100 μL of PBS to prevent the cells from drying out.
Turn on the confocal laser scanning microscope, excitation lasers (405 and 561 nm), and image acquisition software.
Select a 20× objective lens (UplanSApo ×20, numerical aperture: 0.75) and focus on the sample.
Set two channels with parameters for excitation and emission as specified.
Set image resolution to 1024 × 1024-pixels with 1× digital zoom (pixel size: 0.62 μm) and scan speed to 20 μsec/pixel.
Adjust Airy Units to 7.67 AU for Alexa Fluor 405 and to 5.25 AU for PI.
Set LUT to Hi-Lo mode and click “Live” to display fluorescence signals.
Tune up laser powers such that both channels show substantial levels of fluorescence signals without saturation.
Set a ROI for image acquisition to cover the central part but exclude the edge in each field of view (with a 20× objective lens, typically set a ROI of 695 × 695 pixels near the center).
Acquire fluorescence images from a single focal plane.
Select at least three different positions for imaging in each well.
Ensure that the selected position contains over 50 cells.
Perform image analysis using MATLAB to semi-quantify the amount of 6-4PPs in each cell.
Assess the kinetics of removal of 6-4PPs through image analysis.
Split multichannel images into individual fluorescence images.
Save individual fluorescence images as TIFF files.
Open and display the acquired fluorescence images with MATLAB.
Open the image of PI fluorescence.
Binarize the image of PI fluorescence using MATLAB code.
Remove noise and fill gaps in the binarized fluorescence image.
Demarcate cell nuclei from the processed image.
Distinguish attached cell nuclei by watershed conversion.
Discriminate remaining attached cells and signal noise based on circularity and area of each cell nucleus.
Binarize the fluorescence image of PI to determine ROIs corresponding to individual cell nuclei.
Remove the signal noise and fill the gap in the nucleus.
Label each ROI.
Distinguish attached cells by watershed conversion.
Remove nuclei that are small or located at the edge of the image.
Obtain information on the morphology of individual ROIs.
Calculate the area, bounding box, centroid, perimeter, and pixel index list for each ROI.
Determine circularity by calculating 4*pi*area / perimeter^2 for each ROI.
Evaluate circularity and area of the ROIs to remove attached cells.
Create a binary image for false-positive regions based on evaluated criteria.
Create a binary image for true-positive regions based on evaluated criteria.
Display DNA-adjusted image with boundaries marked in red and green for false-positive and true-positive regions, respectively.
For each ROI, calculate mean fluorescence intensity per pixel of 6-4PPs relative to that of PI.
Divide the mean fluorescence intensity of Alexa Fluor 405 by the mean intensity of PI for each ROI.
Open the work space.
Copy and paste the relative intensity of 6-4PPs in each cell into an Excel file.
Calculate the median of the relative intensity of 6-4PPs in each image.
Prepare a standard curve using the medians.
Determine the amount of 6-4PPs after recovery culture for the indicated time periods.
